sections.content: How many people are "waste disposal and environmental services managers"?

13,195 people

were counted on the census as "waste disposal and environmental services managers" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Waste disposal and environmental services managers organise and co-ordinate the operations and development of waste disposal and related environmental services facilities within private firms or public authorities.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "waste disposal and environmental services managers" there were more men than women (83.5% compared with 16.5%).

This means "waste disposal and environmental services managers" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "other managers and proprietors".

Men made up 83.6% and women made up 16.4% of "waste disposal and environmental services managers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "waste disposal and environmental services managers" included:

  • assemblers (vehicles and metal goods)
  • engineering project managers and project engineers
  • plastics process operatives

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "waste disposal and environmental services managers", 16.4% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "waste disposal and environmental services managers" was 16 to 19 years.

  • managers in transport and distribution
  • office managers
  • health and safety managers and officers

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "waste disposal and environmental services managers", 8% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (85.9% compared with 14.1%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (75.4%) than self-employed (24.6%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Copeland, this is in the region of the North West.
